senses.gloss: (b. h; cmp. דלל) to be light, slender.—זוֹלֵל, v. זוּל.
to treat lightly, to despise, neglect (with ב).
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 6b:22">Ber. 6ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 12:9">Ps. XII, 9</cite>) <he>ובני אדם מְזַלְזְלִין בהן</he> and which people treat slightly. Y. Peah I, 15ᵈ, sq. <he>מז׳ בבני וכ׳</he> they despise the sons of the handmaids; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 84">Gen. R. s. 84</cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 62b:13">Sabb. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>המְזַלְזֵל וכ׳</he> he who is neglectful in the observance &c.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 36a">Ab. Zar. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>לודאי מזלזלין הן</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>דמזלזלו</he>) the Lyddeans are neglectful of religious observances; a. e.

senses.gloss: ז׳ מעות to disregard money-matters. Y. Snh. VIII, 26ᵇ top; ib. XI, beg. 30ᵃ (the rebellious son that took what belonged to his father) אינו חייב עד שיְזַלְזֵל מ׳ cannot be made responsible, unless he disregards money, expl. ib. ‘he takes an object and sells it for its exact cost price’ (thus proving both his rationality and his wastefulness).
